en: The Mantra Rite of Mañjuśrīyamāntaka:
At that time, the World-Honored One was dwelling within the Bamboo Grove in the city of Rājagṛha together with Mañjuśrī.
They engaged in a discourse concerning the causes by which he had encountered the Buddha Dīpaṃkara in the past and received his prediction of enlightenment. At that time, there was a great...
The Vajra Yakṣa General then rose from his seat amidst the assembly,
bared his right shoulder, and placed his right knee upon the ground.
Joining his palms toward the Buddha, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, regarding the Dharma now being taught by you together with Mañjuśrī concerning matters from past lives:
World-Honored One, for how many kalpas did you practice the dhāraṇī methods of the Wrathful Kings while on the bodhisattva path?"
To speak briefly now:
in his final birth, he attained Buddhahood with the name Shanhui (Good Wisdom) and received a prophecy from the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara.
He is named Śākyamuni Buddha.
When he subsequently appears and attains Buddhahood in this Sahā world,
may I manifest great majestic power within this realm.
Because he sought to subdue all stubborn and haughty people,
the Buddha Dīpaṃkara immediately understood my intention:
"I now act for the sake of sentient beings in future ages."
After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, at the time when the Buddha-dharma is extinguished,
during the time of great terror and the evil age,
when all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas have vanished and are no longer seen.
For the sake of protecting the Buddha-dharma;
for the sake of the world’s stable abiding;
and for the sake of subduing all wicked people.
The punishment of those who destroy the Buddha-dharma is for the sake of employing skillful means to bring sentient beings to maturity,
and for the sake of perfecting the inconceivable conduct of a bodhisattva.
In order to eliminate the karmic obstacles of inconceivable sentient beings,
and for the sake of sentient beings in future generations when the Buddha-dharma is about to perish.
If one is able to receive and uphold this rite for the wrathful king Mandāravatī according to the Dharma,
that person will certainly attain accomplishment immediately.
At that time, it was for the purpose of punishing the wicked ācāryas;
it was intended to punish those evil persons who lack compassion,
and was not originally for the sake of good people.
This was spoken solely for the purpose of subduing those who corrupt the Dharma,
not for those who harbor desires directed toward themselves,
but for the sake of protecting the Buddha-dharma.
At that time, when Vajrapāṇi had spoken this Dharma,
the Buddha remained silent and entered the Buddha-transformation samādhi.
Then the youth Mañjuśrī also remained silent and spoke no word.
The great earth shook in six ways;
the entire assembly, along with all devas and humans, were utterly terrified, as were the dragon kings,
the *dhana* spirits, the *mātṛkā* goddesses, the *graha* spirits, and others.
As well as all evil beings, such as the Bhūtas, Piśācas, and Apsarases,
all shall be struck with fear and take refuge in the Dharma King.
We pray that the World-Honored One and the youth Mañjuśrī will protect us out of compassion.
This mantra was extremely terrifying;
it scorched and boiled [them], causing them such suffering and distress that they fell to the ground in a stupor, unable to distinguish east from west.
At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī cried out in a loud voice, saying:
"You gods, nāgas, the eight classes of beings, humans, and non-humans,
do not give rise to fear.
I now intend to establish the Great Teaching here."
Those who universally practice and apply this according to each of my teachings should, with a heart of great compassion,
bring to mind the emanation body of Śākyamuni Tathāgata, the Honored One among two-legged beings.
If the wrathful king Yamantraka enters the Samādhi of Fierce Agility,
the sublime supernatural powers and majestic radiance of even tenth-stage Bodhisattvas are entirely extinguished.
How much more so for you all— the devas, nāgas, the eight classes of beings, humans, non-humans, and all who are auspicious—
if you hear me, the Great Wrathful King, proclaim this great divine mantra.
Terrified and bewildered, they lost their sense of direction;
yet they remembered all the dhāraṇīs spoken by the Buddha,
including the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa dhāraṇī and the Vairocana-cakra-ekākṣara-rāja dhāraṇī.
The *Śatru-ghāta-viśatru-uṣṇīṣa* and other spells;
the spell of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva;
the *Vijayā-kūṭa-tārā-bhañjana-rakṣasī-mahāśrī-vidyā-jayavati-haya-karṇa-rāja* and other such spells.
This mind is called the mantra, the most supreme of all.
If one can recite the mantra of the One-Syllable Cakravartin King,
it is the most supreme among the aforementioned mantras.
All devas, nāgas, the eight classes of beings, humans, non-humans, and so forth—
by reciting this even once,
Yamantraka shall be unable to disturb or harass them.
Regarding the mantras you have now spoken— namely Māmaki, Śaṅkhāra, Sikhara-vajra, Kuru-dā-muṣṭini, Rāśanada, and so forth—
the Vajra retinue will likewise provide protection through their mindfulness.
By recollecting the mantra of the Bodhisattva Constant Fragrance King, the mantra of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra,
and others, one shall likewise obtain protection and freedom from fear.
The Maṇibhadra mantra.
The śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas must likewise maintain mindfulness and offer worship, remaining free from fear.
This applies even to those such as the Śrīgha-parā devas and the kings of the formless realms who have transcended desire.
Through mindfulness, one also attains fearlessness;
one should constantly mindfully recollect and make offerings to the Triple Gem,
and always have faith in the Buddha-dharma.
Such persons shall remain free from illness for the rest of their lives;
Yamāntaka shall be unable to harm them.
Those who are able to uphold this [mantra] must not give rise to thoughts of retreat.
Regarding the method for painting images:
if there are evil persons who seek to extinguish the Buddha-dharma,
one need not consider whether the day is auspicious or inauspicious, nor need one attend to the positions of the stars or constellations.
Either on the fourteenth or the eighth day of the dark fortnight,
one should take a garment from a corpse in a śmaśāna;
it is even more excellent if one obtains the garment of a brāhmaṇa.
Take blood and dye it;
thereafter, wash it again and dry it in the sun.
Then, commission an artist to paint the image.
This image, painted by himself, is the very best.
Its countenance is so fierce that it strikes fear into people.
It was painted within the Śītavana cemetery.
It must be completed within three days.
On the fifteenth day of the dark fortnight, take the fat of a deceased person to serve as lamp oil.
The mantra-practitioner faces south, while the image faces north.
Recite the mantra to bind the boundary;
the mantra-practitioner sits upon a *kapāla* (skull-cup) to perform the rite,
and immediately during the first watch of the night, he contemplates the tormenting of enemies and malicious persons.
In the second watch, he will suffer from a cruel affliction, becoming distressed and disoriented, unable to distinguish the directions.
In the third watch, he will fall to the ground in a state of total exhaustion.
However, if the mantra-practitioner rejoices and turns his heart [toward compassion], the patient will be cured.
If the mantra-practitioner does not turn their compassion toward the place where the wicked person lies suffering from illness,
that person will only be subjected to further idle talk by others.
This person’s body will wither and die,
and their house and possessions will all be destroyed and scattered.
Such is the ritual procedure.
Its image has six faces, six hands, and six feet;
it is black in color with a slender waist, adorned with *kaparda* ornaments.
Its facial expression is wrathful and fierce.
His hair stands straight up like flickering flames, pointing upward;
his eyes are red as blood,
and his body is covered with tiger skin.
Holding a *pātra* and various weapons in his hands,
he has three eyes;
his body is smoke-colored or the color of black clouds.
He assumes a terrifying form,
riding upon a water buffalo,
and is able to cause all beings to feel fear.
When painting this image,
use blood mixed with pigments for the red;
place ox fat and human fat inside a human skull.
Harmonize the colors.
Take the hair of a deceased person to serve as a brush.
Once the image is completed, perform extensive offerings.
Rub the mandala with red sandalwood;
use red flowers for the offering;
take the fat of a dead person to serve as the lamp.
The flesh of a dead person was used as incense.
He made offerings three times each day and,
upon completing the painted image, he paid the full price for its labor.
Do not allow the painter to harbor resentment;
you must provide him with abundant wealth and goods.
Thereafter, the mantra-practitioner will swiftly attain accomplishment and achieve complete perfection through the recitation of mantras.
If one performs the ritual for protecting the body and reciting mantras without accordance with the Dharma,
one will ultimately be harmed and killed, and one's six kin will perish until the entire family line is extinguished. However,
if one practices in accordance with the Dharma, [the opposite shall occur].
By this, one immediately obtains protection.
One who constantly maintains [the practice] according to the Dharma will thereafter achieve success in all desired ritual activities performed in various places.
If one performs these acts solely for the purpose of extinguishing the Buddha-dharma,
they will indeed be extinguished without remainder. However,
if one performs them for the sake of one's own minor affairs, such acts must not be done.
In this present life, it swiftly brings about untimely retribution;
in future lives, it brings about the fruits of hell.
For those who wish to obtain the fire-burning rite:
Install the image in a purified location with its face turned toward the north.
In front of the image, construct a single-ground hearth.
The size [of the fire] may be as one wishes.
Burn dry wood, thorns, needles,
and *saoji* (soapberry) fuel while reciting the Yamāntaka mantra.
To invoke the Fire Deity, use the seal of King Yama.
In this manner, first perform one thousand and eight recitations while burning [the offerings].
Throughout, one must maintain a state of wrath and mentally call out the name of the evil person.
One will immediately achieve the success of the ritual procedure.
First, there will be the death of both husband and wife;
second, the death of the wife as well as the extinction of all their kinsmen and attendants.
In the third watch, that evil person dies.
Furthermore, if one recites the mantra oneself with the intent to destroy an enemy, the entire family of that enemy shall be extinguished.
If one recites the mantra at midnight, the entire kingdom shall likewise be utterly destroyed.
Either celestial deities send down fire to burn their kingdom,
or there is excessive rain with no clearing of the skies,
or foreign lands and others inflict punishment upon that kingdom.
Either an era of famine arises,
or a celestial thunderbolt kills people,
or an epidemic breaks out within the nation.
Some may die with their bodies withered and parched;
or spirits and demons may harass and disturb their palaces, chambers, and dwellings day and night, causing them to sleep uneasily.
Rākṣasas, yakṣas, insects, wolves, tigers, and leopards shall not cease their activities all day long, constantly harassing and terrifying them beyond measure.
Where even Maheśvara, Brahmā, Śakra, and the worldly deities cannot provide protection or rescue,
if the mantra-reciter’s mind of anger does not cease,
there is no one at all who can save those who stand before him.
If one recites the mantra day and night without ceasing, constantly mindful of its recitation and never forgetting it,
one will attain the power to subdue the people of Jambudvīpa.
On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight...
One should install the image in a śītavana (cemetery),
in a forest retreat (araṇya),
or beneath a solitary tree in a remote location.
Some were placed in stone caves;
some were placed in empty huts;
and some were placed within large temple halls.
Either place it upon a seashore,
or place it in a solitary, uninhabited location,
and install the image therein.
Once the image has been consecrated, the performance of the ritual methods yields inconceivable results.
This mantra method of the wrathful king Yamāntaka is also inconceivable;
the practitioner who achieves mastery through the recitation of the mantra is likewise inconceivable.
Even all the bodhisattvas are unable to protect [him],
let alone Maheśvara and others who might be able to protect him; for Yamāntaka punishes evil persons.
Moreover, even all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas cannot take away [the power of] the mantra of Vajrapāṇi used to subdue and punish evil people.
If the mantra-practitioner does not turn back from his anger, there is no liberation.
If one wishes for this person to be freed from suffering, the mantra-master must direct a mind of compassion toward them.
Furthermore, there is another method: take *kaṭuka* leaves, white mustard seeds, oil, poison, human blood, human flesh, salt, and *hūṅ* (barley malt).
Pippalī, dry ginger, mustard seeds, and *vatsaka* are ground into a powder;
this is combined with the juice of jujube fruits,
wine, and sea salt.
The *nāḍuka* root, the *kuśa* root, the *kīka* root,
the *bimba* root, the *yavakṣāra* root,
barley ash, the *jambū* flower, and the *mātuluṅga* root.
Garlic, leeks, and *palaśa*—
all these aforementioned medicines should be taken in equal parts.
Before the image, recite the mantra once for each portion and burn them.
If recited one thousand and eight times,
it can eliminate enemies along with their retinues.
This medicinal rite should be performed during the first watch of the night.
If one arrives in a land under martial law where famine and pestilence have arisen, and it is filled with yakṣas and rākṣasas;

where fires break out on all sides and hail falls, slaughtering the kingdom, cities, towns, and villages until they are utterly destroyed; and where various kinds of misfortunes afflict the native country—all such signs portend that the punishment will fall upon one's own nation.
Furthermore, there is a method: take *nada* roots;
recite the mantra once and burn one root, repeating this one thousand and eight times.
Evil persons will then become deluded and deceived.
Furthermore, take the three pungent herbs and recite the same mantra as above one thousand and eight times;
immediately the evil person’s body and mind will be tormented with feverish distress, and they will not know what course of action to take.
Furthermore, take an *āmalaka* fruit and recite the same mantra over it one thousand and eight times;
this will immediately cause the person's body to tremble with cold.
Either after two days or seven days and seven nights,
the person before one shall receive the retribution of withering.
If one wishes to perform the fire rite, one should first form the *śakti-mudrā*.

Furthermore, there is another method: if one knows the deity to whom a person belongs or the constellation to which they belong, one should take charcoal from a cemetery (śītavana) and draw the form of that stellar deity.
One should write the name of the person in question beneath the feet and place it before the painted image.
The mantra-practitioner steps upon the person's head and recites the mantra with wrath;
the person immediately contracts various diseases,
or dies, or if they do not die, their illness becomes grave.
The same applies to those possessed by malevolent spirits or their retinues.
At that time, the Vajra Yamanṭaka,
having prostrated at the Buddha’s feet within the great assembly, remained silent.
Furthermore, for the benefit of sentient beings,
he again expounded the dhāraṇī methods and the rites of accomplishment for the yakṣiṇīs;
these were taught for those with lustful desires and for those seeking wealth and treasures.
Those who cannot rely on the Buddha's teachings,
who do not understand the practice of contemplation,
and who do not understand the arising of dhyāna.
This is spoken for those who have been transmigrating in birth and death since beginningless time and are unable to feel weary of it or seek liberation from it.
Those who perceive the nature of phenomena and penetrate the underlying principle do not wish for this state of existence.
Thereupon, he spoke a mantra, saying:
Oṃ īrṣyāntari mahānāgani hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. This dharma-mantra should be recited regularly every night after midnight, rising for the purpose, without limit as to the number of repetitions.
When the full month has passed and he no longer sleeps,
at the end of that month,
the yakṣa-rākṣasī will come to him and become his wife.
Whatever he sought was immediately fulfilled.
Every day, twenty-five gold coins were sent to him,
along with long-life elixirs.
At that time, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of yakṣas, rākṣasas, and yakṣiṇīs shall all achieve success in the Dharma.
One need only recite the Yamāntaka mantra and perform the ritual before the image.
"May all those who require this, whether gods, ghosts, or those with aspirations, assemble here.
May those who seek it quickly obtain its fulfillment.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva prostrated at the Buddha’s feet.
In the presence of the Buddha, he then recited the mantra of Yamāntaka for the purpose of punishing evil persons and subduing sentient beings.
He spoke the mantra as follows:
Namaḥ samantabuddhānām | Apāvṛtasarvabuddhamudrāṇām | Namaḥ pratyekabuddhāryaśrāvakāṇām | Namaḥ sarvabodhisattvānām | Dharṣayami ||

*svāhā*. At that time, the Great Vajra addressed the devas, saying:
This King of Wrathful Kings, Yamāntaka,
is able to subdue the various punishments and disciplinary measures of King Yama,
and is likewise able to subdue all mantras as well as the mantras of the celestial sages.
Furthermore, it can subdue those who curse evil persons or act contrary to the Dharma,
as well as the ten-stage Bodhisattvas and the worldly mantra-deities.
At that time, through immeasurable power, all the functions and accomplishments described in the ritual methods of the wrathful king Yamāntaka are realized.
If one who maintains this Yamāntaka Wrathful King merely recites this mantra,
they will also be able to bring all other mantra-deities and the like under their control.
By reciting and contemplating this Yamāntaka Wrathful King mantra with single-minded devotion, one shall attain accomplishment.
Namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvānām | apratihataśāsanānām | oṃ kara kara kuru kuru mama ṭiri ṭiri jñāpa jñāpa sarvavighnān naha naha ||1||

This is the root mantra of Mañjuśrī; within this rite, it must always be used for binding the boundary and protecting the body.
At that time, Mahākrodhavajra surveyed the four directions and,
observing the great assembly, wishing to further proclaim the dharmas of wrath, addressed them, saying:
"O you hosts of devas and all you spirits and ghosts who dwell in reliance upon the dharmadhātu!"
When one wishes to perform the ritual,
first form the *khaṭvāṅga* mudrā to protect the body so that the signs of accomplishment may be swiftly attained; then,
perform the fire ritual (*agnikārya*).
This shall cause all spirits, demons, and the like to be completely subdued, so that they dare not inflict harm.
When performing the rite,
first take up an image depicting wrathful anger.
Install [the image] within a temple of Maheśvara.
Take poison, red mustard seeds, fat, and blood;
mix these together with bitter nimba leaves and offer them to the painted image.
The mantra practitioner takes the intestines and belly of a corpse and lays them crosswise;
the mantra practitioner then takes the *kāpāla* (skull) of the corpse from his own person while reciting the mantra.
With the left hand, he forms the mudrā of the aforementioned *kalpa*;
with the right hand, he carves the head of Maheśvara.
The mantra-practitioner, filled with wrath, visualizes the aforementioned evil person who has insulted and oppressed himself and others.
Those who are arrogant due to wealth and status, those with evil associates,
those who are formidable, those possessed of abundant riches and treasures,
and such individuals as high-ranking ministers and nobles.
Immediately perform the aforementioned rite: close the door, sit naked, and if you are a lay practitioner, let your hair hang loose and step with your left foot upon Maheśvara.
If you can recite the mantra, the body of Maheśvara will naturally split into two pieces.
If a roar like that of a bull issues from the air,
the mantra practitioner should not fear it out of anger; rather,
he should firmly settle his own mind.
On that very day, Dharāja and the others were possessed by tigers and demons,
or by evil spirits and rākṣasas;
yet as he further recited the mantra, even those wicked men all gave up their lives.
If one recites the mantra at night, all members of the household and their kin will likewise [be protected].
Furthermore, there is another method: throughout the day, go to the temple of Īśvara.
Fasting for one night,
on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, one takes wood from a śītavana (cemetery) tree and kindles a fire.
One then takes red mustard seeds together with blood, poisons, and other such substances.
With each incantation and each burning, a great voice will issue forth from mid-air.
At that time, all the hungry ghosts (preta) will assemble and appear before the mantra-practitioner;
one must by no means feel fear.
The mantra-practitioner replied to the aforementioned hungry ghosts, saying,
"Exterminate my enemies and wicked people.
The ghosts replied to the mantra-practitioner, saying:
It will surely fulfill one's wishes and then vanish, remaining unmanifest.
Evil persons for hundreds or thousands of *li* shall not speak ill of one;
all enemies, whether near or far, as well as ghosts and spirits, shall all be utterly extinguished.
In a single moment of thought, all shall be completely cured,
and their kinsmen shall all be dispersed.
Such dharmas as these, involving immeasurable rites, shall all be accomplished.
Furthermore, in a pure place such as an empty house or a vacant dwelling,
wearing clean garments,
one should take a piece of white cotton cloth from within.
Recite the mantra once for each burning, completing one thousand and eight repetitions.
With both hands, scoop up the ashes from the aforementioned folded paper,
and immediately wrap them in a clean cloth.
Take two earthen bowls and place a lump of ash in each;
then recite the mantra and perform the ritual to protect the body.
Then, on the eighth or fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, the mantra-practitioner shall face south and cast the two bags of ash toward the Śītavana cemetery.
Place two earthenware bowls filled with ash in front [of the practitioner]. The mantra-adept,
naked and with disheveled hair, revealing his form, stands with feet planted firmly and an expression of wrath.
If one recites the mantra ten thousand times, one will immediately attain accomplishment.
Among the ghosts and spirits therein, if any should demand the previously mentioned ashes,
one must by no means give them to them.
If ghosts or spirits forcibly seize the ashes,
one should immediately recollect the one-syllable mantra of Yamāntaka.
The mantra is as follows:
Upon uttering the sound "HŪṂ," all spirits and ghosts were completely dispersed and extinguished;
all obstacles were entirely purified and eliminated.
If one takes its ashes, one should immediately mark them on the left and right;
one must never become confused or forgetful,
and thus one should inscribe the marks for both the left and the right.
The mantra-practitioner must not be negligent.
While reciting the mantra, one must certainly protect the body.
This continues until the sky becomes clear and the sun rises.
He immediately bathed, put on clean clothes,
and returned home.
Upon arriving at his house, he then took the medicine held in his right hand and applied it to protect his body.
All ghosts, humans, and quadrupeds,
as well as all sentient beings such as devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and so forth—
by immediately scattering this ash upon the devas, nāgas, spirits, humans, and others, they shall be brought under control.
If one scatters the ashes held in the left hand upon a man or woman, they will immediately be brought under control.
If one scatters the ashes held in the right hand upon the aforementioned person,
it will cause that person's private organ to wither and fail to become erect.
It is like a eunuch;
if one places it upon the private parts of an ordinary person,
one is unable to engage in sexual intercourse.
If it is scattered upon a woman’s birth canal,
she will be unable to engage in sexual intercourse with her husband,
as the birth canal becomes obstructed.
Just as when the husband engages in sexual desire,
her birth canal opens of its own accord,
whereas it cannot possibly open for anyone else.
At that time, the man’s conduct was likewise.
When he asked others, he would immediately obtain his own intended wife.
If one were to scatter this ash upon all men and women, regardless of whether they were noble or lowly, [the same result would follow].
This ash grants the power of subjugation and allows one to act according to one's will.
If a woman applies this ash, her birth canal will open,
and she will be brought under control to act according to one's will.
If a woman applies this ash and forcibly engages in sexual desire,
maggots will emerge from her birth canal,
and the birth canal will become putrid and foul-smelling like the scent of a corpse.
The woman passed away after one month;
the husband’s male organ likewise became like that of a woman, and he suffered the same kind of pain before passing away later.
Furthermore, if the mantra-adept’s heart gives rise to a sense of affection and desire,
he may obtain [his goal]. If there are evil persons in whatever direction or at whatever place the adept seeks,
he should then take this ash and scatter it with his hand along the path of the wind.
One will immediately obtain one's wish;
this may be achieved whether performing it oneself or sending another to do so,
and even at the place where one sits or lies down.
All furnishings upon the beds and seats, all ornaments,
garments, coverlets,
and rugs— everything whatsoever.

Furthermore, the heart-mantra is spoken as follows:

Oṃ tīrthakālupe hūṃ khaṃ svāhā. This mantra possesses great power and is capable of accomplishing all tasks. Yamāntaka Vajra has taught the various mudrās of the *mudrā-kula* (the section on seals) and the binding of all protective seals.
First, extend the ring finger of the left hand toward the tiger-mouth (the base of the thumb).
Do the same with the right hand.
Then, interlace the two little fingers and direct them into the space between the ring fingers.
Place the two middle fingers upright outside the "tiger's mouth" with their tips touching;
bend the two index fingers so they rest upon the joints of the middle fingers;
and hold the two thumbs straight up against the middle joints of the middle fingers.
This is the seal that binds all;
it is the summoning seal.
It follows the previous seal.
Pointing downward with the two index fingers is called the Summoning Seal (ākarṣaṇamudrā).
The Great Vajra Seal (mahāviśvavajramudrā).
Following the previous seal, extend the two index fingers straight upward, half an inch away from the middle fingers;
this is called the Great Cross Seal (Mahāśūla-mudrā),
the Seal of Offering.
Place the middle finger of the left hand behind the ring finger;
with the thumb, press the upper joint of the ring finger, while the index and little fingers are slightly bent.
With the right hand, hook the left index finger with the right index finger.
Hook the left little finger with the right middle finger.
Curve the tips of the right ring finger and index finger into the palm.
Press the thumb against the nail of the little finger.
This is called the incense burner mudrā.
For the mutual overcoming mudrā:
interlace the two hands.
The five fingers are bent within the palms.
The right thumb is raised, while the left thumb presses against the third joint of the ring finger.
This is called the *parasparābhimardana-mudrā* (the seal of mutual pressing).
The *kṣepa-mudrā*.
It is performed according to the previous *anyonya-lalita-mudrā*,
with the exception that the two middle fingers are raised and joined together.
This is called the Nāgapāśa-mudrā,
the seal for subduing all wicked people.
It is performed according to the previous method, with the right thumb bent into the palm.
This is called the Seal for Subduing All Evil Persons.
To form the seal,
follow the previous procedure but change it by holding the two thumbs upright.
This is called the Seal of the Raised Staff.
The Seal of the Iron Arrow is used for the subjugation and punishment of all enemies.
As before, hold the seal;
however, the two thumbs are slightly separated.
This is called the Iron Arrow Seal (ayaḥśara-mudrā).
The Tooth Seal:
Furthermore, join the two hands together with the five fingers held straight up;
bend the two ring fingers into the palms.
Place the thumb upon the second joint of the ring finger;
bring the tips of the middle fingers close to the two little fingers respectively;
then cast [the hand] according to the seal.
Furthermore, join the palms of both hands together,
extend all five fingers straight upward,
and rotate this mudrā across the chest from left to right.
Make a gesture toward the right;
pull it toward the left.
This is the Mañjuśrī Yamāntaka rite.
